text:
cheng: Heads-up — after the driver bump pushed to the Eu-West2 Hopper pool last night (driver 535.89) we started seeing throughput drop and a handful of PTX/JIT failures for SM90 kernels. Noticed ~25-40% throughput regressions on the tx-heavy chat routes. pinging @maria @alex for visibility and @raj for ops.

maria: saw the same in the dashboards at ~02:11UTC. p50 latency for 8k-seq models jumped 28ms -> 45ms, p95 spiked 120ms -> 300ms. Retry loop increased token cost ~18% on the hot routes. I created an alert (infra.hopper.euw2.driver.regress).

alex: attaching a representative snippet from the canary node logs:

```
[2026-03-17T02:09:13Z] model=redwood-small kernel=sm90 compile_status=error
ptxas fatal   : Unsupported ptxopt version / failed to link module
error: ptx linking timed out after 30s
warning: falling back to interpreter kernel
-- cudalog --
E 02:09:13 ptx_compile: /usr/lib/nvidia/ptxas: exit 1
E 02:09:13 loader: failed to load cubin for kernel 'self_attention_fwd'
```

Also grabbed nvidia-smi from that host: `Driver Version: 535.89` and CUDA runtime 12.3. Ops-level note: NCCL seems fine but kernel selection ends up choosing slower codepath.

raj: ops notes — we pushed 535.89 as default because it fixed an H100 nvlink handshake in us-west. Didn't expect SM90 ptx differences to surface. We have a canary group (20 nodes) in eu-west2 that got the update.

maria: short-term mitigation: 1) rollback the eu-west2 canary to the previous driver (533.74) 2) pin driver min for hopper-pool in eu-west2 to 533.74 in provisioning manifest 3) throttle heavy seq routes or shift weight to us-west2 where driver is still 533.x.

ops-bot: Rollback runbook created: https://internal/runbooks/infra/driver-rollback. Runbook id RB-2026-045. (action required)

deploy-bot: Canary rollback job started (job id: deploy-9876) — rolling 20 nodes back to driver 533.74. ETA ~18m.

alex: quick cost estimate — if eu-west2 continues at current retry rate we'll burn an extra ~$600/day on the hot account. If this persists into a week, that's ~4k. Also CPU fallback kernels blow out power/perf.

raj: adding additional context: we saw two failure modes: (A) PTX link timeouts during JIT, (B) kernel selection that drops to interpreter path for a subset of fused kernels. Both increase per-token latency. Suspect a PTX optimizer flag change in 535.x interacting with our custom fused kernels for SM90.

cheng: agreed on rollback. After rollback we should: - run full canary suite (latency + perf + regression evals) - revert driver bump in artifact repo and add stricter compatibility tests for SM90/PTX in CI - open infra ticket to schedule a staged re-roll with a patched PTX pipeline.

maria: assigning follow-ups: INFRA-3421 pin provisioning manifest (raj), INFRA-3422 run canary perf suite (alex), INFRA-3423 cost impact + temporary routing (maria).

alex: +1 to CI tests. I can add a quick integration that runs PTX link on our fused kernels under 534/535 ranges. Will start today.

raj: rollback finished on canary at 02:28UTC. Early signals look good — p50 back to ~30ms, p95 trending down. Monitoring for 30m then we'll decide to roll the rest. :thumbsup:

cheng: nice work. Keep the channel updated on the full fleet decision. Also lets add a short postmortem link once we have root cause. :thinking:

maria: I'll open the postmortem draft (PM-2026-11) and include timeline + cost delta.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback completed (deploy-9876). All 20 canary hosts now on driver 533.74.

ops-bot: Created ticket INFRA-3424 to track staged rollout plan and compatibility fixes.

alex: leaving logs + repro steps in the ticket. If anyone sees a node with the 'falling back to interpreter kernel' message, please pin and tag me.

cheng: thanks all. We'll regroup after the 3pm ops sync. :fire:
